summary: A flat white fuel canopy with a red brand stripe stands on four slim columns over two pump islands. Behind it is a low flat-roofed store: a glass-fronted white shop under a red sign fascia and cantilever awning, beside a taller grey service block. A red-and-black price pylon stands at the street corner. The canopy, the pumps under it, the pylon and the glass shop behind the forecourt make it read as a gas station at a glance. Flat white canopy with a red stripe on four columns over two pump islands. Behind it, a white glass-front store with a red MART fascia beside a taller grey service block. A red-headed price pylon, an asphalt lot and the forecourt fittings complete the site.

Store shell: Store shell built in parts/shell.mjs: shop and service walls, floors, black plinth, piers and mullions, red sign band, partitions. All openings and reserved cells are left unwritten (air). make.sh gives a whole build.nbt with no refused writes, no off-palette blocks and no floating blocks, and all five rooms are walkable.
polish: Roof part reports off-palette blocks (smooth_stone_stairs, andesite_slab, stone_slab); roof.json needs fixing
Glazier must fill the storefront glass, doors, the west window band and the slot glass at (28,2..6,25)
Shop walls are y1..5 and the red band is y5. The y6 red parapet and the decks come from the roof tool
Store shell: still OFF-PALETTE: smooth_stone_stairs x40 (roof.json), andesite_slab x40 (roof.json), stone_slab x64 (roof.json)

waste.what: Hand-wrote an openings-list predicate to skip writing cells, because carve() stores air and locks it
waste.cost: one local helper, 14 boxes
waste.tool: A runParts-aware 'hollow box with openings' helper that skips opening boxes without writing air

companions.task: Fill the storefront bays, doors and transom, the west window band and the slot glass

summary:
Roofs: Roofs part built: shop flat-parapet roof (y6) from roof.json and service block roof (y8, x24..32 z24..33, no west overhang) via roof() in parts/roofs.mjs, with palette-only stone materials and a rooftop rail.
Two hvac_unit rooftop units at (26,28) and (29,28) on the service deck, y9..10.
make.sh saved a whole build.nbt; Roofs part placed 202 cells with 0 refused and 0 off-palette; check reports 0 floating and 0 unsupported; renders read as flat roofs with the taller service block and HVAC.
polish: ROOF_SINGLE_MATERIAL warning on both flat decks (the deck reads as one tone); a flat deck is intended, so left as is.
The shop roof's north overhang at z=23 sits at y6..7 and the keep box protects the MART lettering cells, but the lettering part must still check it lands on those keep cells.
The service roof is laid in parts/roofs.mjs rather than roof.json because runParts takes one roof spec with a single y; plan.md Notes records this.

waste.what: Testing roof material variants one at a time: stone, mix and trim choices each needed a dry-run to see which blocks came out off-palette (smooth_stone_stairs, andesite_slab, stone_slab from the modern preset defaults).
waste.cost: About 4 dry-run cycles on roof.json
waste.tool: A `mcd roof --spec ... --dry-run --palette palette.json` mode that lists off-palette blocks and suggests the palette-matching trim/eave/ridge per preset, plus the keys the spec's material object accepts.

waste.what: The second roof at a different y had to be hand-wired in roofs.mjs because runParts lays one roof.json; the spec keys (footprint, keep, overhang per side) were worked out by reading roofs.mjs.
waste.cost: About 3 minutes reading roof() options and writing a direct call
waste.tool: runParts accepting a list of roof specs (roof: ["roof.json", "roof-service.json"]) or a per-footprint y in the roof spec, with the spec keys documented in references/toolkit.md.

waste.what: Checking that the built roofs sat at the planned heights and leave the keep cells alone was done by eye from the tiles.
waste.cost: Two render views and a check run
waste.tool: A `mcd roof --detect`-style report per roof that prints its eave y, footprint and keep-cell clearance against plan.md.

companions.task: The rooftop rail (iron_bars) and the HVAC unit housings and lids, so the rail posts and unit lids land cleanly on the deck.
The coping and parapet courses on the shop and service decks, to choose the slab and stair pieces so the coping reads as cut stone and matches the polished andesite trim.

summary:
Fuel canopy and pumps: Fuel canopy and pumps built in parts/canopy.mjs: canopy_deck x6..34 z9..20 (y7..9, sea_lantern grid, red stripe), 4 canopy_column stubs, pump_island A/B with yellow bollards, 4 fuel_pump units at z14..15.
make.sh saved a whole build.nbt: canopy part placed 878, refused 0, off-palette 0. Tiles read as the plan's canopy.
Ticked plan.md PARTS item 3 and elements.md's four canopy items (canopy deck, columns, islands, pumps).
polish: check reports 10 'unsupported' attachments: the 8 flush sea_lantern soffit lights at y7 (x10,16,20,24,30 on z12/z17 per plan) plus 2 others; they sit under the y7 soffit with air at y8, which the check reads as hanging from nothing. Plan puts them flush, so this is a planner-level flag, not a fix in this part.
fuel_pump has no lever nozzle; the elements item says 'hose = iron_chain/lever side', and the vocab helper only writes an iron_chain hose. Left as the helper builds it.

From the north the pumps sit under the fascia and are hidden behind the columns in the zoom; they are placed exactly per plan (z14..15, y2..4) but read weakly at street level, as in the concept where they are more visible.

waste.what: Checked each helper's footprint by reading its source (scope boxes, LIGHT_X/LIGHT_Z offsets) to confirm plan coordinates before writing the module.
waste.cost: about 3 tool calls and roughly 2 minutes of reading
waste.tool: A vocab index that lists each helper's footprint box and the cells it writes, e.g. `$MCD vocab --footprints`, so a worker can confirm coordinates without reading source.

waste.what: Ticked plan.md's PARTS item and four elements.md checkboxes by hand, one Edit per line.
waste.cost: 5 Edit calls
waste.tool: A `mcd tick <file> <pattern>` command, or a make.sh step that ticks items from parts-report.json.

waste.what: Counted expected placed cells by hand (deck, ring, columns, islands, pumps) to sanity-check the 878 total from the report.
waste.cost: a few minutes of arithmetic that did not change the result
waste.tool: A per-part census in parts-report.json broken down by element, so the count can be checked against the plan without arithmetic.

companions.task: Own the canopy soffit light grid: decide whether the flush sea_lanterns at y7 (air above) should get a support or a different fitting, so the structure check stops flagging them.
Build the pump nozzles and hose detail (lever nozzle, hose curve) on the red heads so each pump reads as a pump from the street, not only as a white column with a screen.

summary:
Openings and signs: Openings and signs (parts/fittings.mjs) built: shop glazing on z=24 with the main double door and transom, slot glass, awning, MART letters, service logo panel, canopy roundel, and the east and south rear doors.
make.sh produced a whole build.nbt. The part reports 90 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette, and the front render reads the storefront, door and awning correctly.
Open items: the slot-window black frames (x27/x29, z24) are the shell's gray wall cells, so they were not built. The roundel floats until the canopy deck is built next to it.
polish: Slot window frames: black_concrete at x27 and x29, z24, y2..6 are not built. The shell left those wall cells gray_concrete, and the part below is locked, so slot_window skipped them. Needs a shell change or a replace pass in a later part.
The canopy roundel at x19..21 y7..9 z8 floats in the current build; it touches the canopy fascia at z9 once the canopy part is in, so the check should be rerun after the canopy merge.
The shell's storefront walls and the store block glass item in elements.md stay unticked: the glass is built, but the block around it belongs to the shell.
Service block item in elements.md stays unticked: the logo panel and slot glass are built, but the frames are still missing.

waste.what: Worked out which cells the glazed bays, transom, door and awning take by hand, then checked each one in the render. The transom over the door needed a second storefront_bay call on the door columns, found by trial.
waste.cost: about 4 tool calls and 2 renders
waste.tool: A helper like storefront_bay(g, x0, x1, z, {doorAt, transomY}) or a glazing(g, ...) that takes the door and its transom in one call, so the door cells and transom are not split across calls.

waste.what: Door material id: B.door takes the bare material name and appends _door, but I first passed iron_door and the report flagged iron_door_door x4. Fixed by hand.
waste.cost: 1 failed build and 1 retry
waste.tool: Document the B.door id convention in the toolkit reference, or have the rear-door call use glass_double_door-style single-door helper.

waste.what: Single rear doors (east and south) are hand-written as two g.set calls each, with half and hinge set by hand, because no single-door vocab helper exists.
waste.cost: 4 g.set calls
waste.tool: A single_door(g, x, z, facing, {hinge}) helper alongside glass_double_door, returning both halves.

waste.what: Used sed -i on macOS without the '' suffix, which failed and wasted a call.
waste.cost: 1 retry
waste.tool: Use the Edit tool for in-place edits of plan.md and elements.md checkboxes.

waste.what: Ticked elements.md and plan.md checkboxes one line at a time, and wrote the Notes entry by hand.
waste.cost: 2 bash calls
waste.tool: A mcd tick command that marks an element done by part number and matches its item name.

companions.task: Set the slot window's black_concrete frames at x27 and x29 in the shell's gray wall, with the replace pass needed to change the shell's cells, so the frames sit proud of the gray wall as plan.md specifies.
Lay out the MART letters and the logo panel with a set letter grid and the roundel's centre, so the letters read as MART from the street and do not depend on hand-placed spacing.

summary:
Site and grounds: Site and grounds built in parts/grounds.mjs: street with dashed centre line, smooth-stone sidewalk with two asphalt curb cuts, forecourt and front-lane asphalt, store apron, west parking with three stalls, verges with short grass and dandelions, three birch trees, the z=36 hedge, two light poles.
make.sh builds a whole build.nbt: my part placed 1209 blocks, 0 refused, 0 off-palette. mcd check: no floating or unsupported blocks, walkable end to end. The tiles show the street, sidewalk, curb cuts and apron where the plan puts them.
Ticked plan.md item 5 and the matching elements.md items; added a Notes line on the clipped birch and on replace for ground repaving.
polish: Other parts' issue, not this part: roof.json puts off-palette blocks into the Store shell (smooth_stone_stairs x40, andesite_slab x40, stone_slab x64). make.sh reports it on the shell line; it needs fixing in the roof spec.
The tree at (40,0,16): only the part of its crown inside the lot is built (the x=42 cells are off the grid). If the plan wants the full crown, the grid would need to grow.

waste.what: The east birch (40,0,16) has a crown that runs past x=41, so birch_tree throws on the out-of-bounds cell. I wrote a local clipped birch() by hand.
waste.cost: One failed make.sh run plus a rewrite of the tree routine (about 15 lines).
waste.tool: birch_tree (and the other tree/crown helpers) should clip to the grid, or take a bounds option, instead of throwing.

waste.what: Ground surface writes: the helpers only write into air unless told to replace, and the ground is grass_block from build.mjs. I had to work out which helpers need { replace: true } and which (centre_dashes, parking_stall) only paint over asphalt, and then order the asphalt before the paint.
waste.cost: About six reads of helper sources to learn the replace/paint rules before the first build.
waste.tool: A ground helper such as repave(g, box, block) that declares it overwrites the y=0 base, plus a note in the vocabulary comments saying paint helpers only lay over gray_concrete_powder.

waste.what: Scattered short_grass, dandelion and coarse_dirt patches were picked cell by cell with a hand-rolled loop and hand-chosen patch coordinates, avoiding tree trunks.
waste.cost: About 15 coordinates written by hand plus one seeded loop.
waste.tool: A scatter(g, box, {blocks, density, avoid, seed}) helper that places plant and ground patches on a surface and skips listed cells.

waste.what: Verified the sidewalk/curb-cut/apron layout by eye from the front-left tile only; no overlay of the plan's coordinates on the render.
waste.cost: One render plus one look; no plan-vs-build cell check for the parking and pole positions.
waste.tool: mcd plan-diff, or a 'mcd zoom --at' check against plan.md's coordinates for each element of the part.

summary:
Forecourt fittings: Forecourt fittings built in parts/forecourt.mjs: price pylon (37,8), air station (36,23), ice chest (25,23) and propane cage (28,22), dumpster enclosure (35..39, 29..33), EV chargers at (1,25) and (1,28), all via vocab helpers (156 blocks placed).
make.sh finishes with a whole build.nbt; this part shows no REFUSED writes and no OFF-PALETTE blocks. Zoomed renders read as a pylon, air post, ice chest with cage, and EV posts.
Four elements.md items ticked (pylon, air/water, ice/propane, dumpster); the EV chargers sit inside the shared parking item, which is left for the grounds part.
polish: The shared 'Parking, 3 stalls' item in elements.md (P5 parking_stall plus my EV chargers) is left unticked for the grounds worker to close.

`mcd check` reports 6 UNSUPPORTED sea_lantern cells at x38..39 z7 y5,7,9 (the pylon digit rows). They are face-attached to the black board at z8, so this looks like a false positive: the checker's hanging-block test matches the 'lantern' in sea_lantern. Exit code is 0. Left as is, to be fixed in the checker, not in the build.
The pylon digit rows are blank sea_lantern bars, not readable price numerals. Fine at glance distance, but a sign-writer would be needed for real digits.
Roofs part (P2, not mine): the roof tool emits OFF-PALETTE smooth_stone_stairs x40, andesite_slab x40 and stone_slab x64, so roof.json needs palette-legal ids. Reported by make.sh.
plan.md Notes not edited; this part did not need a new helper, and the sea_lantern checker note belongs there for whoever runs the checker.

waste.what: Worked out each helper's (x, z) argument by translating plan.md's footprints by hand (for example, price_pylon's x0 is the panel's west cell, not the footing's; propane_cage's 2x2 origin versus the plan's x25..30 span).
waste.cost: about 6 coordinate conversions, plus one re-check against the plan
waste.tool: A plan.md table that gives the helper call and its arguments per element (for example `price_pylon(37,8)`), or a `mcd plan --calls` that prints them, would remove the conversion step.

waste.what: Checked each forecourt element by eye with separate zooms (pylon, forecourt overview, EV chargers from west, air station), 4 renders in all, to confirm placement and that each element reads as itself.
waste.cost: 4 zoom calls plus reading each image, about 3 minutes
waste.tool: `mcd zoom` accepting several --at points in one call, or a named-feature contact sheet built from the plan's element list, would give one image to check.

waste.what: Investigated the 6 UNSUPPORTED sea_lantern warnings to confirm they were a false positive (the blocks are face-attached to the board at z8, and the render agrees).
waste.cost: one check run, one block lookup, one zoom
waste.tool: `mcd check`'s hanging-block heuristic should treat sea_lantern as a full cube; it currently matches the 'lantern' name.

waste.what: Used sed to tick elements.md, which failed in the shell, so I switched to the Edit tool and read the file first.
waste.cost: one failed command and four Edits
waste.tool: A `mcd tick <file> <item-substring>` helper would tick checklist items in one call.

companions.task: Paint the price digits on the pylon's black board as readable numerals (sea_lantern/white stroke font) instead of three bars of lantern blocks, and letter the fuel-price rows.
Fit the air/water station's hose, gauge and lever so it reads as a working air station, and rig the propane cage's cylinders and chain as a proper stand.

summary:
room: Sales floor: Sales floor furnished in parts/room-1.mjs: checkout counter (red front, quartz top) as the focal piece just inside the main door, a coffee corner with cauldron and standing lantern, three 1-wide N-S shelf runs with flower-pot stock, and a glass cooler wall on the south.
Light: 5 hanging lanterns under the roof deck (one over the counter). Walk is OK, 104/104 floor cells reachable, min light 8, no dark or dim cells.
make.sh runs whole and clean for this part (75 blocks placed, no REFUSED, no OFF-PALETTE); check shows 0 floating blocks; render and room.png look as intended.
polish: Stock-room lane: the sales floor's east wall at x=23 still closes the interior doorway at (24,1..2,30), so there is no route from the sales floor to the stock room. The shell part needs to open x=23 at z=30 (or move the doorway); I did not touch the shell.
Elements.md 'Interior' item covers all five rooms, so I did not tick it; the sales floor part is built.
Roof spec (roof.json) reports OFF-PALETTE blocks: smooth_stone_stairs, andesite_slab, stone_slab. This is the roofs part's problem, not this room's, but it still needs fixing.
Plan.md's wall-to-stock lane note cannot be met from this box until the shell opens x=23.

waste.what: Drew the 13x8 floor grid by hand as text rows and converted absolute x/z to string indices (x-10, z-25) for every furniture cell; rewrote the lantern rows after one index slip.
waste.cost: about 4 full-layout rewrites and one miscounted row fixed by hand; the layers() origin arithmetic was done in my head
waste.tool: `mcd plan` could emit the furniture legend and a ready-to-paste layer template with the origin and the 'o' cells already keyed, or layers() could accept absolute {x,y,z:char} cells so no index arithmetic is needed

waste.what: Hand-set pane connection states (east/west true) for the cooler glass band and worked out which lantern spots clear the dim cells by reading the light grid.
waste.cost: 2 extra make/room cycles
waste.tool: `mcd room` already prints lantern spots; a `--apply` or a pane helper that sets connections from neighbours in a row (B.pane with auto-connect) would avoid the hand state

waste.what: Checked the rooms.json stock-room doorway by reading the plan grid: x=23 is still a wall between the sales floor and the stock doorway at (24,z30), so the lane to the stock room cannot be built from inside my box.
waste.cost: one plan read; no fix possible in my part
waste.tool: `mcd plan` should flag doorways whose approach cell is blocked by a wall (here x=23 separates the room from the door at x=24)

companions.task: build the shelf runs and the checkout counter as joinery (fixed shelf heights, counter top height and the staff-side fitting) so the bases and tops match a real shop fit-out rather than my generic light-gray blocks.
set the cooler glass band (pane connections, mullions and the cooler door, if one is wanted) so the pane states come from the glazier's layout rather than hand-set east/west flags.

summary:
room: Restroom A: Restroom A furnished in parts/room-2.mjs with layers(): basin cauldron and white mirror pane on the north-west corner, barrel with a standing lantern beside it, toilet (smooth-quartz stair seat, light-grey tank) in the south-west corner; the lane from the door stays clear.
Room check says OK: walk reaches every floor cell, light min 10, mean 11.9, 0 dark cells. make.sh saved a whole build.nbt with 7 blocks placed, no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE lines for this part, and check reports 0 floating or unsupported blocks.
polish: plan.md has no per-part checkbox list, and elements.md's 'Interior' item covers all four rooms, so I left it unticked; only Restroom A is done.
The room render from above shows only the shell's exterior, not the furniture, so the look was judged from the room check's floor and light grids, not a picture of the interior.

The toilet stair's facing follows the toolkit doc (facing = side of the full-height back, so 'west' puts the back on the wall). Vanilla may read the other way; a render with the roof in place should confirm it.
The mirror pane's north and west connection states were set by hand and are not render-checked.
The lantern is standing on the barrel because no roof or ceiling exists yet in this test build; once the roof is laid, a hanging lantern could replace it.

waste.what: Restroom A furniture was drawn by hand as three text layers and the legend was set up by hand.
waste.cost: About 3 layers and 7 blocks, plus one pass to get the row indices right.
waste.tool: A `mcd plan --draw` option that emits a furniture template for a room, with a legend keyed by the room's furniture role (fixture, seat, light), would have saved the index work.

waste.what: Checked the look by eye from room.png, but the image shows only the shell exterior from above and no interior.
waste.cost: One render, no usable interior view.
waste.tool: `mcd rooms --cut` or an interior eye view option that cuts the roof and shell at the room's ceiling, so an empty or stub neighbour doesn't hide the room.

waste.what: Worked out the mirror pane's connection states by hand (north/west true against the walls).
waste.cost: A few minutes of reasoning, unverified in the render.
waste.tool: A helper such as `pane_connections(g, x, y, z)` that reads the neighbours and sets each side from the solid blocks around it.

companions.task: lay the smooth-stone or quartz floor and the wall tiling as a border course, so the restroom reads as tiled and not as bare shell.
check the cauldron basin and toilet pair against the drain and water runs, and say where a real supply would come from, so the fittings are plausible rather than just placed.
confirm the lantern spot once the ceiling is laid, and choose between a hanging lantern from the roof deck and the standing one on the barrel.

summary:
room: Restroom B: Restroom B is furnished in parts/room-3.mjs: a seat-stair toilet and a cauldron basin on the north wall, a dispenser hand dryer on the east wall, and a barrel bin in the south-west corner. The door cell (30,27) and the lane stay clear.
Two lanterns hang at y4 on iron chains from the y8 ceiling, over the basin and the barrel.
make.sh produced a whole build.nbt with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE lines for this part; `mcd room` says OK (8/8 cells reachable, min light 10, 0 dark).
polish: plan.md has no per-part checkbox list, and the elements.md 'Interior' item covers all five rooms, so I did not tick it; it is for whoever assembles the parts.
Only the 'from above' view rendered (rooms --out): the shell walls hide a 2x4 room, so I could not read the furniture by eye; the walk and light checks are the evidence.
The roof tool reported OFF-PALETTE blocks (smooth_stone_stairs, andesite_slab, stone_slab) in roof.json; that is the roofer's part, not mine.

waste.what: Worked out the floor-cell coordinates and the lantern/chain column positions by hand from the plan grid.
waste.cost: about 6 coordinate checks and one rewrite of the module
waste.tool: A `mcd room --suggest` mode that proposes fixture cells per room from the floor grid and light map, so the furnisher only picks the pieces.

waste.what: Checked block states one at a time with `mcd states` (cauldron, dispenser, lantern, barrel, stairs, chain).
waste.cost: 5 separate CLI calls
waste.tool: `mcd states` accepting several block ids at once, or a state list in the `plan` output for the palette.

waste.what: The 'rooms --out' render shows only the from-above view and the walls hide the 2x4 interior, so the look was a judgement from the text grids, not a picture.
waste.cost: one render that could not show the furniture
waste.tool: An interior eye view for small rooms in `mcd rooms` (or with --cut the roof off), not only the from-above view.

companions.task: Plumbing for the basin and toilet (a water cauldron or a sink look that reads as a basin, with the toilet's tank) so the fixtures read as working, not as stand-in blocks.
Confirm the chain lanterns hang from a real ceiling at y8 once the roof is laid, and check the light map after the roof is in.

summary:
room: Hall: Hall (parts/room-4.mjs): one hanging lantern at (28,7,27) over the lane's junction; the three floor cells stay clear, all reachable, light 8-9 at the feet with no dark cell.
make.sh exits 0 and writes a whole build.nbt; the Hall line shows 1 placed, no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE.
The lantern is unsupported: nothing is at y8 above it, because the service-block roof deck is not built (roof.json covers only the shop footprint at y6).
polish: Lantern (28,7,27) is UNSUPPORTED until a block sits at (28,8,27): the service-block roof deck at y8 (x24..32, z24..33) is missing. roof.json only has the shop footprint at y6, and the plan's second roof spec for the service block is not written. The roofs part must add it; `$MCD check build.nbt` flags this one lantern.
If the service deck cannot land at y8, the Hall has no supported light; the fallback is a different light fixture in a palette block, which the lamplighter must choose. I did not invent one.

No sign or focal piece: signs and item frames are not in palette.json, and the one-wide hall has no floor room for furniture without blocking the lane. The focal point is the centre lantern at the junction.
plan.md has no checklist with ticks (its PARTS list is untagged), and elements.md's 'Interior' item covers all rooms, so I did not tick it; only the Hall is built.
roof.json's OFF-PALETTE report (smooth_stone_stairs, andesite_slab, stone_slab) comes from the roofs part, not from this module; I left it alone.

waste.what: Worked out which y-layer was the ceiling by writing a throwaway node script that printed block layers y6..8 around the Hall, because the room check only says 'nothing above to hang from' and does not show what is above.
waste.cost: 2 tool calls, about 1 minute; a per-layer grid of the block near the cell.
waste.tool: A `mcd layers build.nbt --box x0,y0,z0,x1,y1,z1` (or `room --cells`) that prints the block names per layer over a box, and says which roof deck is missing, would have shown the ceiling gap at once.

waste.what: Had to read the full make.sh log and the roof.json footprint to learn the service deck was absent, instead of the build reporting that a planned roof is missing.
waste.cost: 2 tool calls.
waste.tool: make.sh / runParts should report each roof spec's footprint against the plan's roof list (it had 1 roof spec for 2 planned roofs).

companions.task: Lay the service block's flat deck at y8 (x24..32, z24..33, parapet y9) with its own roof spec, so the Hall's hanging lantern at (28,7,27) has a block to hang from.
Confirm the Hall's light source once the ceiling exists, and choose a palette light for the case where the deck cannot be built.

summary:
room: Stock room: Stock room furnished in parts/room-5.mjs: barrels and chests along the walls, a receiving desk (oak_planks) with a standing lantern in the NE corner as focal piece, a cauldron mop bucket, and three standing lanterns on the tops for light.
Walk check OK: 21 of 21 floor cells reachable; light min 11, no dark cell. Clear lane along z=31 plus all four doorway first cells.
make.sh finished with a whole build.nbt; the Stock room line shows 12 placed, no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE. `mcd check` reports 0 floating and 0 orphans.
polish: No shelving: the palette has no trapdoors or stairs I used, so the shelf-on-wall idea was dropped. Could add oak_slab shelves over barrels on the north wall.
The interior is hard to read in room.png at this scale: the furniture is small and the above-view is dark. The zoom from outside shows only the closed shell, as expected.
elements.md's shared 'Interior' item and plan.md's checklist were not ticked: that item covers all five rooms, and only the stock room is done.
Lantern hanging state is standing (hanging false) on barrels, chests and the desk; no ceiling lanterns, since the room tool reported light >= 11 without them.

waste.what: Drew the 7x3 furniture grid by hand and checked lane clearance (doorway first cells) cell by cell before writing it.
waste.cost: about 10 minutes of planning and one layers() draft; no retries needed
waste.tool: mcd plan could print a per-cell 'lane must stay clear' overlay (doorway first cells and the lane route) so the furnisher can draw around it without working out the cells by hand

waste.what: Checked the interior by eye through room.png and a zoom, which show the shell rather than the furniture, so the look check tells little.
waste.cost: 2 renders, both unreadable for the interior

summary:
lamplighter: room: Restroom A: Restroom A lit with its existing standing lantern on the barrel (26,2,25): 0 dark, 0 dim, min light 10, mean 11.9, walk verdict OK. No change to parts/room-2.mjs; no second lamp added.
Ceiling confirmed: the y8 bottom-type polished_andesite_slab over the room is a sturdy top face, so a hanging lantern at y7 would hang from it.
Hanging-lantern alternative tested in scratch copies: one hanging lantern at any spot leaves 1-3 dim cells (min 7), so it needs two lamps to match one standing lantern; the standing one stays.
polish: No edit to parts/room-2.mjs: the designer's standing lantern already gives full light, so a lamp at the end of build(g) would duplicate it. The make.sh build.nbt is current.

mcd room's walk counts the tops of furniture as floor cells (25,3,28 above the tank; 25,4,25 above the mirror; 26,3,25 above the lantern) and reports them unreached; the verdict is still OK, but the count is inflated.
mcd room's lamp suggestion 25,4,25 'lantern on the floor against the wall' is a spot above the mirror, not a floor spot; do not follow it.
Off-palette roof blocks from the shell/roof stage (smooth_stone_stairs, andesite_slab, stone_slab) are reported in parts-report.json; not this part's concern.

waste.tool: mcd room --lamp x,y,z,hanging=true|false (a what-if that prints the light and walk verdict without writing a file), or mcd light --try

waste.what: Read the ceiling cells above the room one block at a time with a scratch Grid probe to confirm the y8 slab's type and that it is a sturdy top face.
waste.cost: 1 probe script, 2 calls

summary: lamplighter: room: Restroom B: Restroom B lit with no changes to parts/room-3.mjs: two hanging lanterns at (31,4,25) and (30,4,28) on iron_chain y5..7 under the y8 roof slab. Light map after the roof is in: 8 floor cells, min 10, mean 11.5, 0 dark, 0 dim, walk OK. make.sh produced build.nbt.

Roofs: make.sh reports OFF-PALETTE roof blocks (smooth_stone_stairs x40, andesite_slab x40, stone_slab x64) from roof.json. The roofer needs to fix roof.json; not touched here.

Restroom B's chain ceiling is a bottom polished_andesite_slab at y8 (the roof tool's cap), not a full block. The chains attach to its underside and check reports no issue, but a full-block deck would read more solidly if the roofer changes it.

waste.cost: 1 script, 6 cells read, 1 retry for the import shape
waste.tool: mcd room (or mcd check) could print, for each hanging lantern, the block it hangs from (its chain anchor), so the designer's ceiling check is one command.

companions.task: Replace the off-palette stair and slab blocks the roof tool laid (smooth_stone_stairs, andesite_slab, stone_slab) with palette blocks in roof.json, and say whether the y8 ceiling should be a full block.
Give the 8 canopy sea_lanterns at y7 a block above them or a supported fixture, since mcd check flags them as unsupported.

summary: lamplighter: room: Hall: Hall lit: the hanging lantern at (28,7,27) is confirmed (y8 bottom slab ceiling above it). Part now has a palette fallback: if (28,8,27) isn't built, a sea_lantern sits flush at (28,7,27), held by the x27/x29 side walls. Hall min light 9, 0 dark cells; make.sh builds build.nbt.

summary:
inspection: Fixed the seams between parts: the shop's west window band was an open hole (now glazed), the roof cornice took the awning's back row (roof keeps those cells clear, awning now 2 deep), and the roof spec used off-palette blocks (now palette-only, deck changed to uniform polished andesite). Paths are lit (sidewalk, curb cuts, apron, drive, stalls) with two extra poles and two flush sea lanterns; the walk is ok for all five rooms.
make.sh passes and writes build.nbt; no refused writes or off-palette blocks in the final build.
polish: MART sign (fittings, mart_letters): the 2x2 font reads poorly (A and R are partial, T has no bottom row). vocab/h2.mjs's own comment says the band needs a taller design. Not changed.

Roof deck: the spec now uses polished_andesite with texture:false, so the mixed stone/andesite slab texture is gone. Restoring the texture needs stone_slab, andesite_slab and smooth_stone_stairs added to palette.json, which is a palette decision for the user.

Dark cells still on block light 0 at feet level (about 45): the street z0..4, the back strip z34..37, and a few verge cells at x0..1 z14..16 and x41 z16. I counted the street and back strip as road and lot edge, not paths or courts, so I left them.

mcd check flags 10 sea_lanterns as UNSUPPORTED (8 flush in the canopy soffit, 2 flush in the paving). They are full flush blocks, so this looks like a checker false positive, not a structural problem.
Restroom A: the walk verdict is ok (5 of 5 floor cells reached). The 3 listed unreached cells are the tops of the toilet tank and the mirror/lantern, not floor. Left as is.
Final state was checked by map and walk, not by a re-render after the last edits. The last render was taken before the window, awning, roof and light changes.

waste.what: Scanned build.nbt for blocks outside palette.json by writing a throwaway script; the make report only names off-palette ids from roof.json and gives no coordinates.
waste.cost: 3 scan runs plus 3 roof.json rebuilds to find which roof texture option removes the off-palette blocks.
waste.tool: mcd check build.nbt --palette palette.json, listing each off-palette id with its cells; mcd roof --spec roof.json --palette palette.json as a dry run that names off-palette ids before the full build.

waste.what: Read blocks plane by plane (z=23, z=24, z=22, x=9, x=24, x=32, z=33) with a throwaway script to see the cornice, awning, window hole and door positions.
waste.cost: About 8 plane maps, each read cell by cell into a letter grid.
waste.tool: mcd plane build.nbt --z 24 --x 8..33 --y 0..9, returning a coded grid with a legend (the same as the light and walk output).

waste.what: Counted dark cells per zone (street, sidewalk, drive, stalls, verges) by parsing the text output of mcd light --y 1, and the first parse was off by one column.
waste.cost: 2 parse runs, one with a column offset bug.
waste.tool: mcd light build.nbt --y 1 --box x0,z0,x1,z1 --json, giving the dark count and cell list per box.

waste.what: Found the awning/cornice clash only by reading the z=23 plane: the roof's cornice occupies the awning's back row, and an awning replace call did not overwrite it. The refusal was not reported.
waste.cost: 2 builds and a reverted edit to learn that runParts' lock blocks later writes into roof cells.
waste.tool: A seam report from runParts that names every write refused by the lock (part, cell, and the owning part), and a check that compares each part's footprint against the cells the earlier parts placed.

waste.cost: 10 flagged cells checked one by one.
waste.tool: mcd check should treat flush full blocks such as sea_lantern as supported, and tag a warning as a hanging fitting only for lanterns and chains.
